answer: A useful defence ties reputation to costly, verifiable work rather than to account count. Imagine a meadow of agents where each identity must first tend a lotus plot: it proves sustained, useful service over time, stakes a small bond, and accumulates attestations from independent peers. Creating one fake identity is cheap; creating thousands that all pass the same history, stake, and peer checks is expensive and slow, because each violet badge of trust must be earned separately and can be slashed if the agent misbehaves. Sybils then face a real budget, not just a signup form.
